design.decision: Bid your [K]s as likely winners and lead them early; your own [A]s are the only ones left, so bid more aggressively.
design.opponent: Very visible: their [A]s become [2]s before they bid, so they bid lower and must find tricks elsewhere. It is a deliberate defensive piece against a runaway leader.
design.rationale: The brief favors defense and comebacks in a lopsided game, and this is the strongest visible defensive hand change; the uncommon uc-opp-twos is random and weaker. Departures: it reveals one fact about the opponents' hands (they hold no [A]s), and it can feel bad to the other team; both are accepted to test whether a strong suppression piece reduces runaway leads.

design.hooks: Text template for an Opening 'become' that has both whose=opponents and a from filter ('Opening: Every [A] the opponents hold becomes a [2]'); the kernel already applies whose to BecomeFrom, so only text and simplicity need it.

critic.concerns: It hard-counters an opponent's whole Ranks build (bought [A]s and become-[A] enablers) with no way to respond, and it reveals that no other [A]s are in play (an information departure the designer accepts).
